Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second half! Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran are the openers. Trent Boult to begin.
... The run chase ...

New Zealand will be very pleased with where they've got to! At one stage they were struggling when they were 4 down for around 120 but then came the stand which changed the tide. A stunning partnership between Latham and Glenn Phillips. The two took their time, got used to the pitch of the surface and accelerated towards the end. Afghanistan could have stopped the carnage easily with some bright fielding. Now, they have a stiff task ahead of them. A couple of their batters are in form but need someone to play a big innings. Join us back in a while.

Afghanistan will be very disappointed with how this innings panned out. They had a really good chance to keep New Zealand near 250 but poor death bowling and dropping around 4 catches have cost them. Afghanistan failed to even grab some sitters. The likes of Tom Latham,  Will Young and Glenn Phillips made the most of it. All three scored fifty-plus and pushed New Zealand over 280. New Zealand build their innings well. Even they could have scored more but twice in the innings lost wickets in heaps. However, with the bowling they have, they will be very confident to defend it down.
FOUR! Strong finish from New Zealand. On a length and on middle, Santner hammers it down the ground for a boundary. New Zealand finish with 288.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for the action to begin! Out walk the Kiwi openers, Will Young and Devon Conway. Mujeeb Ur Rahman has the first new ball in hand. Here we go...
Time for the National Anthems now! The players make their way out to the middle. The first ball isn't far away.

Pitch report - Sunil Gavaskar says the Kiwis managed to beat Bangladesh on this surface. Simon Doull adds, it seems a really good pitch, not a lot of grass and the wrist spinners might come into play.

Tom Latham says he wasn't sure what he wanted to do. Adds it is about adapting to the conditions. Informs Young comes in for Williamson. Reckons the wicket might be better than the last one. Ends by saying he hopes they can continue to do well.

Hashmatullah Shahidi says they will bowl first. Adds that there might be dew later on. Adds they'll try and restrict them to a low score. Informs they are playing the same side. Ends by saying they enjoyed their last win but are looking forward to this game.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Ikram Alikhil, Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Naveen-ul-Haq, Fazalhaq Farooqi.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Will Young, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (C) (WK), Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Mitchell Santner, Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the toss and will BOWL first.

Both sides have momentum by their side. The Kiwis, along with India, are probably playing the best brand of cricket so far. Afghanistan on the other hand, have just beaten the World Champions quite convincingly. They'll be looking to cause yet another upset. They are a dangerous side and might just enjoy these conditions here in Chennai. If they play to their potential this should be a close encounter. Toss and teams in a bit.

It is time for match 16 of the 2023 World Cup and the action shifts to Chennai. It is a clash between Afghanistan and New Zealand. With two sides high in confidence, this should be a cracker of a game.
... Match Day ...

Match number 16 is upon us and it will be New Zealand going up against Afghanistan in Chennai in what is expected to be an exciting clash. The Kiwis have continued their form from the last World Cup and are making their way bravely through the league stages. They have already emerged triumphant against England, Netherlands, and Bangladesh without breaking a sweat. The setback they received in the last game is that Kane Williamson suffered a fracture on his thumb after he was hit by a throw while running and is ruled out for the coming fixtures but might make a return towards the end. Will Young might get a chance in the playing 11. Their bowling unit is troubling the batters with the likes of Matt Henry, Mitchell Santner, Trent Boult, and Lockie Ferguson all being equally involved. The batting unit has also proven to be dependable even in the absence of Kane Williamson. Devon Conway started off the World Cup with a strong 152-run knock against England. Rachin Ravindra is at his best after being promoted up the order. He is turning out to be the find of the season. He already has a century and a half-century in this tournament. Will Young also seems to have found his form with Daryl Mitchell and Tom Latham supporting down the order. All in all, this is a team that is looking very strong and certainly, one of the contenders to fight for the top 4 spots on the points table. Afghanistan had started their campaign with a couple of losses with some poor performances but bounced back strongly, upsetting the reigning champions England after the Afghans clinched a 69-run win over them. The team seems to have found their form back. Rahmanullah Gurbaz is brilliant at the top of the order and is scoring some quick runs. Ibrahim Zadran on the other hand seems to be struggling a bit and the Afghans will hope he gets back to form. The skipper, Hashmatullah Shahidi had a good outing against India and built a good partnership with Azmatullah Omarzai but in a losing cause. They must have gained a lot of confidence from that match as they got their first win in the next one. The spin wizards, Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Rashid Khan have also found their rhythm and clinched 6 wickets among them. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Naveen-ul-Haq are taking the pace attack to the batters and need to take timely wickets. Their performance in the last match has helped them gain the necessary momentum for the rest of their campaign. It is a big challenge for them to occupy a place amongst the top 4 on the table but this team has the potential to cause massive upsets. Will the Black Caps continue their win streak or will the Afghans pull out another win from the hat? The answers lie in Chennai as excitement builds for this 'now' high-octane clash.
